newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, ignores Quebrada woes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, ignores Quebrada woes.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker on late liquidation after the market failed to build on earlier, modest gains and ignored news that Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine output has been sharply cut, traders said.
Quebrada Blanca's general manager James Drake said output at the strike hit facility in Chile has been halved. Current inventory will last a few weeks at the 75,000 tonne a year mine.
Some traders believe the six-day old strike had already been factored into the price of copper.
July COMEX copper settled 1.40 cents weaker at 109.05 cents per pound, traded 111.10 to 109.00 cents. Spot May went out 2.05 cents lower at 109.75 cents.
Volume was light at an estimated 5,500 lots.
LME cash to three months backwardation was slightly lower and narrower by COMEX close at $65/$69.
Trade selling on the day's highs and the lack of any follow through fund buying that was expected with the continued gains in the stock market, prompted some disappointed liquidation, a broker said.
"The underlying market is pretty good," he added.
Traders were also mulling a report from broker Macquarie Equities that Chile's copper production could be affected by power outtages unless there is significant rainfall within a month.
LME stocks rose 1,000 tonnes Tuesday to 148,925 tonnes.
